title: Pyramids & energy transfer
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: How do we calculate how much energy moves up the food chain?
What does the shape of an energy pyramid tell us about an ecosystem?
Is the energy transfer always the same percentage?

explain.say: Today we will look at energy pyramids in ecosystems.
The base of the pyramid shows the producers like plants.
The next level shows primary consumers which eat the producers.
Secondary consumers eat the primary consumers in the food chain.
Energy is lost at each transfer up the pyramid.
Efficiency is the energy passed on to the next level.

faq.q: What is the total energy available at the base of the pyramid?
faq.a: The base represents the total energy captured by the producers, usually from the sun.
asks: Where does the energy pyramid start?
What is the energy source for the bottom level?

faq.q: Why is the pyramid shape always tapering downwards?
faq.a: Because a large amount of energy is lost as heat or used for life processes at every step.
asks: Why does the energy decrease at higher levels?
What causes the pyramid to get smaller?

faq.q: How do I calculate the efficiency of energy transfer?
faq.a: You divide the energy at the higher level by the energy at the lower level, then multiply by one hundred.
asks: What is the formula for energy transfer?
If I know the start and end energy, how do I find efficiency?

faq.q: Can the energy pyramid be inverted?
faq.a: Generally, no, because energy flows in one direction from the sun to the top predators.
asks: Are there exceptions to the pyramid shape?
Can energy flow backwards in an ecosystem?

faq.q: What does 'biomass' mean in this context?
faq.a: Biomass is the total mass or amount of living organic matter at a specific trophic level.
asks: Is biomass the same as energy?
How is biomass measured in an ecosystem?

facts: Producers capture energy from sunlight through photosynthesis.
Energy transfer between trophic levels is not 100% efficient.
A significant amount of energy is lost as heat during life processes.
The efficiency of energy transfer is often estimated to be around ten percent.

quiz.say: If producers have 10,000 units of energy, and primary consumers have 1,000 units, what is the efficiency?
quiz.why: You divide the energy at the next level by the energy at the current level, which gives ten percent.

wrong.0: You cannot add the energy from two different levels like this.
wrong.1: You must multiply by one hundred to get the percentage.
wrong.3: This calculates how much more energy the producers have than the consumers.

quiz.say: Which group forms the base of the energy pyramid?
quiz.why: Producers are the first organisms to capture energy from the sun.

wrong.0: These organisms are higher up the food chain.
wrong.1: Decomposers break down dead matter, they are not the main energy source.
wrong.3: These organisms eat the producers, so they are not the base.

quiz.say: If a pyramid shows energy decreasing, what does this indicate?

options.show: Energy is lost to the environment
options.say: Energy is lost to the environment

quiz.why: The loss of energy as heat or waste causes the pyramid to decrease in size.

wrong.1: Energy loss is normal and expected in all ecosystems.
wrong.2: Energy loss does not mean the chain has stopped working.
wrong.3: Energy loss is due to metabolism, not just producer quantity.
